name: AddActorMessage
summary: Introduce a remote actor into the client's world view. The wire type is 121, NOT 449: the previous 449 pairing came from a name/GUID adjacency false positive, and this file records the correction.
purpose: Presence: without this family of messages peers cannot appear to each other.

lifecycle.if_absent: other players invisible; multiplayer appears empty

fields.name: head16
fields.note: A raw 16-byte fixed-size read. The unmarshal facet FUN_146a6b3e0 begins with FUN_1408787b0(param_2, param_3, 0x10, &ok), and FUN_1408787b0 is a bounds-checked fixed-size read: it checks cursor + n <= end, copies n bytes, and advances the cursor. What is NOT proven is that these bytes are an ActorGuid: nothing in the facet interprets them, and a corpus-wide search found no 16-byte comparison in an actor context. The old 'candidate ActorGuid' label is therefore unsupported and stays a candidate.

fields.name: u8_at_0x10
fields.note: Assigned as a plain byte right after the 16-byte read: *(char *)(param_3 + 0x10) = cStack_38.

fields.name: count_payload
fields.note: FUN_146a6ebe0(&state, param_3 + 0x18, param_2) fills it immediately after the byte at 0x10.

fields.name: tail_from_0x28
fields.note: The facet then reads at 0x28, 0x30, and a nested group through FUN_146a6e090 at 0x38, 0x40, 0x48, 0x50, 0x78, 0xa0 and 0xc8. The 15-field list carried over from the deleted crate is consistent with these offsets but its individual meanings were never decoded.

evidence.ref: wire type corrected 2026-10-25. FUN_146ac20a0 builds the literal name from immediates (lStack_28 = 0x726f746341646441 = 'AddActor', uStack_20 = 'Mess', uStack_1c = 'ag', uStack_1a = 'e') AND parses &UNK_1485800f0, which is the UPPERCASE dashed GUID 96C829CE-DFBC-4763-959C-32A6B22D81EF = typeindex slot 121. One function, both halves, so the binding AddActorMessage -> slot 121 is read from the compiler rather than from adjacency

the false positive's mechanism, measured in .rdata at 0x1485800e0: 'AddActorMessage\0' is immediately followed by the UPPERCASE GUID 96C829CE-... (slot 121) at 0x1485800f0, and only then, after four NULs, by the lowercase GUID bc291efa-... (slot 449) at 0x148580118. scan-wire-names.py searches the LOWERCASE dashed form, so it never matches slot 121's uppercase string; for slot 449 it reads back over the NULs, walks past the uppercase GUID, and keeps the longest printable run, which is 'AddActorMessage'. That is Trap 1 from that tool's own docstring, firing

research/derived/wire-type-names.json is wrong for these two slots as a consequence: it records 449 -> AddActorMessage (source rdata) and 121 -> name null. The correct pairing is 121 -> AddActorMessage and 449 -> unnamed

unmarshal facet FUN_146a6b3e0 (0x146a6b3e0-0x146a6b4b5, 213 bytes), reached from FUN_146a339a0 (0x146a339a0-0x146a33a1c). First statement FUN_1408787b0(param_2, param_3, 0x10, &cStackX_20), and FUN_1408787b0 (0x1408787b0-0x1408787fb) is a bounds-checked n-byte read: if (cursor + n <= end) copy n bytes and cursor += n, else set the failure flag

negative: a corpus-wide scan found only 12 memcmp call sites, none with a 0x10 length and none in an actor context, so nothing corroborates 'the first 16 bytes are the actor id'. The field is measured as 16 opaque bytes and no more
